_comment: Named OpenStreetMap trails added to packs by tools/fetch_map_details.py. Each entry is assembled from all OSM ways carrying `osm_name` (longest connected stretch), elevated from the pack terrain, and classified automatically.

trails.note: Steepest regular trail in the White Mountains: a Class 3 headwall scramble. Not recommended for descent or in wet or icy conditions.
Long, rugged ridge to Mount Madison over the Howks; above treeline on the upper ridge.
Very steep, often wet ledges on the old slide: much easier going up than down.

trails.name: Franconia Ridge Trail (Mt. Flume – Mt. Lafayette)

trails.note: Short Appalachian Trail stretch from Pinkham Notch along the Ellis River to Lost Pond, with views of Mt. Washington across the water.

auto._comment: Every named hiking trail in the region (beyond the hand-picked list above)

Wildcat Ridge Trail.note: Very steep, ledgy climbs over the Wildcat peaks from Pinkham Notch.

Carter-Moriah Trail.note: Appalachian Trail along the Carter–Moriah Range; exposed ledges on Mount Moriah.

White Dot Trail.note: The most direct and most crowded route: steep, sustained rock scrambling above Falcon Spring junction.

White Cross Trail.note: Slightly gentler than White Dot; the usual descent from the Headquarters side.

White Arrow Trail.note: Oldest route on the mountain, from the Old Toll Road / Halfway House site.

Pumpelly Trail.note: Long ridge approach from Dublin with many open ledges.

trails.name: Midstate Trail (Ashburnham–Westminster)
trails.note: Section of the Midstate Trail (yellow triangles), a 95-mile footpath from Rhode Island to New Hampshire; includes short road walks.

trails.name: Midstate Trail (Westminster)
trails.note: Section of the Midstate Trail (yellow triangles), a 95-mile footpath from Rhode Island to New Hampshire; includes short road walks.

trails.name: Midstate Trail (Leominster State Forest)
trails.note: Section of the Midstate Trail (yellow triangles), a 95-mile footpath from Rhode Island to New Hampshire; includes short road walks. Crosses the top of the Crow Hills.

trails.name: Midstate Trail (Wachusett Mountain)
trails.note: Section of the Midstate Trail (yellow triangles), a 95-mile footpath from Rhode Island to New Hampshire; includes short road walks. Climbs over the 2,006 ft summit of Wachusett Mountain with the Harrington Trail.

trails.name: Midstate Trail (Princeton South)
trails.note: Section of the Midstate Trail (yellow triangles), a 95-mile footpath from Rhode Island to New Hampshire; includes short road walks.

trails.name: Crow Hill Trail
trails.note: Rocky trail along the base of the Crow Hill Ledges from the Route 31 lot, with two scrambles up to the ridgetop Midstate Trail; watch for climbers and loose rock.

trails.name: Crow Hill Ledges North Climb
trails.note: Steep, rocky scramble up the Crow Hill Ledges between the cliff-base Crow Hill Trail and the Midstate Trail on the ridge; watch for climbers and loose rock.

trails.name: Crow Hill Ledges South Climb
trails.note: Steep, rocky scramble up the Crow Hill Ledges between the cliff-base Crow Hill Trail and the Midstate Trail on the ridge; watch for climbers and loose rock.

trails.name: Crow Hill Ledges South Loop
trails.note: Woods road looping off the south end of the Crow Hill Trail below the ledges.

defaults.note: Shared with mountain bikers: keep right and listen for riders.

Harrington Trail.note: Steepest route up Wachusett Mountain, shared in part with the Midstate Trail; rocky ledges near the top.

Holy Hill (yellow blaze).note: Loop over the Shakers' Holy Hill worship ground with views across the Harvard orchards.

Nashua Acton & Boston Railroad Trail.note: Level walk on the bed of the old Nashua, Acton & Boston Railroad.

Acton Minutemen Line of March, April 19.note: Route the Acton Minutemen took to the North Bridge in Concord on April 19, 1775.

M&M Trail (white).note: New England National Scenic Trail (white blazes): rugged traprock ridge walking with many short, steep climbs.

NET.note: New England National Scenic Trail (white blazes): rugged traprock ridge walking with many short, steep climbs.

M&M.note: New England National Scenic Trail (white blazes): rugged traprock ridge walking with many short, steep climbs.

RFT (orange).note: Robert Frost Trail (orange blazes), a long-distance footpath from the Holyoke Range to Mt. Toby through Amherst conservation land.

Robert Frost Trail (orange).note: Robert Frost Trail (orange blazes), a long-distance footpath from the Holyoke Range to Mt. Toby through Amherst conservation land.

Appalachian Trail.note: The AT follows the park's crest for about 72 miles; shelters require a backcountry permit and reservation.

Alum Cave Trail.note: Arch Rock, Inspiration Point and Alum Cave Bluffs on the way up Mount Le Conte; steep, cabled ledges near the top.

Chimney Tops Trail.note: Steep climb to an observation point; the summit pinnacles beyond are closed since the 2016 fire.

Abrams Falls Trail.note: Do not swim below the falls — strong currents and deaths have occurred.

Bright Angel Trail.note: Most popular inner-canyon trail; seasonal water at the rest houses and Havasupai Gardens. Every mile down is about two coming up.

South Kaibab Trail.note: Steep, exposed ridge trail with no water and little shade; not recommended for ascent in summer.

North Kaibab Trail.note: Only maintained route from the North Rim; water seasonal at Supai Tunnel, Manzanita and Cottonwood.

Rim Trail.note: Mostly paved walk along the South Rim between South Kaibab Trailhead and Hermits Rest; leashed pets allowed.

Hermit Trail.note: Unmaintained, rocky and steep; for experienced canyon hikers.

Grandview Trail.note: Steep, unmaintained historic mining trail to Horseshoe Mesa; no water.

Mount Washburn Trail.note: Old road to the fire lookout; bighorn sheep are common near the summit.

Fairy Falls Trail.note: Passes the Grand Prismatic Spring overlook on the way to 200 ft Fairy Falls.

Uncle Tom's Trail.note: Steep metal staircase to the base of the Lower Falls.

Cascade Canyon Trail.note: From Jenny Lake via Hidden Falls and Inspiration Point; moose and black bears are common.

Teton Crest Trail.note: Multi-day high route along the west side of the range; backcountry permit required for camping.

Paintbrush Canyon Trail.note: Steep climb to Paintbrush Divide; snow and ice can linger into August.

Ryan Mountain Trail.note: Steep, no shade: start early in summer.

Lost Palms Oasis Trail.note: Long, exposed desert walk to the park's largest palm oasis; no water.

California Riding and Hiking Trail.note: Long-distance trail across the park's high desert; water caches must be arranged in advance.

Avalanche Pass Trail.note: Through the pass to Avalanche Lake; ladders and the Hitch-up Matilda boardwalks along the cliffs.
